methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Problem and Solution
content: Problem: Students often list past events using "and... and... and..." without clear chronological markers, making narratives sound flat and repetitive.
Solution: Introduce the 5 core sequence adverbs (First, Next, Then, After that, Finally) as sentence starters to map out chronological narratives using regular past tense verbs.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: Pull-out oral tasks (teacher does these with 1–2 students while class works):
S1 pull-out: Show sequence flashcards. Student must link two actions orally: "First, I walked. Then, I played."
S2 pull-out: Give a 3-step prompt (wake up, eat, play). Student answers in full past tense using "First, Next, Finally."
S3 pull-out: Student reads S3 VC script. Teacher notes pronunciation errors on sequence words and recasts gently.
Communicative task (Step 5 — 10 min — MUST have real information gap):

Students piece together a 4-step story. Student A has events 1 and 3. Student B has events 2 and 4. They must ask each other "What happened [first/next]?" and write the missing steps to complete the narrative.
Materials needed: Print 2 copies of Card A and 2 copies of Card B from Section 8.
First: Hold up one index finger confidently.
Then / Next: Move hand in a small jump to the right.
After that: Make a sweeping arch motion with the hand.
Finally: Two hands push down flat, signaling the end.
Common errors to watch during pull-out:
Error: Forgetting the comma pause. "First I walked..."
Recast: "Listen: First, [pause] I walked. You try."
Error: Mixing present tense with past sequences. "Next, I play football."
